item.title: Gioele named a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher 2026
item.description: Gioele La Manno has been named a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher in the Cross-Field category for 2026, his third consecutive inclusion following 2024 and 2025. His primary affiliation on the list is EPFL. Announced on 18 November, this year’s list recognises 6,802 researchers across more than 1,200 institutions in 62 countries and regions. Clarivate awarded 7,090 recognitions, including 3,251 in the Cross-Field category. The distinction between researchers and recognitions matters: some people appear in more than one subject category.

item.title: Celebrating the Eppendorf & Science Prize in Washington
item.description: On 15 November 2026, Gioele received the Eppendorf & Science Prize for Neurobiology at the award ceremony in Washington, D.C., during the week of the Society for Neuroscience meeting. The celebration brought together experts in neuroscience, editors from Science, and representatives of Eppendorf. Among those present were Marina Picciotto, Mattia Maroso, Senior Editor at Science and chair of the prize jury, and Axel Jahns of Eppendorf. It was a special opportunity to share the lab’s work and celebrate with the wider neuroscience community.

item.title: Gioele included in the 2026 Stanford/Elsevier top-cited scientists list
item.description: Gioele La Manno is included in the 2026 edition of the Stanford/Elsevier top-cited scientists database, commonly known as the world’s top 2% scientists list. The entry appears in the single-year citation-impact list, based on citations received during 2025, with EPFL as the affiliation and Developmental Biology as the primary subfield. This recognition reflects the continuing use of the lab’s research by the wider scientific community. The database was released on 7 October 2026 using an August 2026 Scopus snapshot.
